title: GitHub - orsenthil/git-hook-model-identification: Git hook enforcing AI model self-identification in commit messages
excerpt: Git hook enforcing AI model self-identification in commit messages - orsenthil/git-hook-model-identification
content_html:
Model Identification hook for Git Commits

It is desirable to have model and model properties identification in git commits authored by AI models. This repository provides a git hook that enforces a commit message format and a review workflow.

Every AI-authored commit carries a one-line self-identification, so a stronger model can review it later and know who wrote it and how sure they were.

A git hook can't instruct a model directly, so commit-msg rejects the commit with instructions. The agent reads the error, adds the trailers, and retries. It works with any agent that runs git commit.

What a commit looks like

Add retry backoff to fetch

Model: claude-sonnet-5-5 harness=claude-code effort=high conf=medium

Full format and rules: SPEC.md.

Install

cd your-repo && /path/to/install.sh     # this repo only (core.hooksPath -> this project's hooks/)
/path/to/install.sh --global            # all repos (copies hooks to ~/.config/git/hooks)

Global install copies the hooks, so re-run it after updating them. It also overrides any per-repo .git/hooks.

Use

  • Agents: commit normally; if rejected, follow the printed instructions.

  • Humans: GIT_HUMAN_COMMIT=1 git commit ... skips the check. Merges, reverts are exempt automatically

Review workflow

post-commit copies the Model trailer into git notes --ref=model-id with Review-Status: pending.

bin/model-review list [range]            # self-ID + status per commit
bin/model-review comment <sha> "<text>"  # reviewer comment -> refs/notes/model-review; marks reviewed
git push origin refs/notes/model-id refs/notes/model-review   # notes are not pushed by default

The trailer in the commit message is the source of truth; notes are an index and can be lost on amend/rebase.

Limits

The identification is self-reported: a model can misstate its own ID or confidence if it is instructed to do so.
